note: A grass opening in the woods at the end of a level dirt driveway of about 170 ft on the west side of Montour Road, 13.6 miles from PA 120; soft after rain. The agency's campsite map layer marks the site as having no trailer access, while the booking page sells it as an RV and trailer site with a 40-ft maximum. Montour Road from PA 120 is a severe climb: about 10% held for 2.6 miles. The better way is from PA 872 by Elk Lick Run Road and Trout Run Road, whose one hard pitch is about 10.5% for 0.8 mile, then 4.6 miles south on Montour Road; Swank Road from First Fork Road holds about 9% for nearly 2 miles. All dirt or gravel forest road, for dry weather. No toilet. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: 061 Bubbling Springs still listed and bookable online, Drive-In, RV/Tent/Trailer categories, 40 ft, clearance 20 ft, dirt pull-in driveway 170 ft (3DEP: level). Access: stated approach ~10% for 4.2 km (far longer than the yardstick); the Elk Lick Run Road approach is about at the yardstick. Reported. Fees confirmed, $6.50 fee added; season written; facilities none. Imagery: a grass opening ~25 m across at the pin with further openings north-west and south; pin on it, not moved. NHD: nothing within 200 m.
flags: DROP CANDIDATE TO WEIGH (ruling 9): Montour Road from PA 120 (the page's own route) climbs 411 m in one unbroken 4.2-km run at a 9.7-9.8% mean (steepest 200 m 11.7-11.9%): the same grade as Spade Road but three and a half times as long. From the north, PA 872 > Elk Lick Run Road 3.8 mi > Trout Run Road 1.5 mi > Montour Road, the one hard climb is 10.5% for 1.35 km on Elk Lick Run Road with the steepest 200 m at 14.3%: about the Spade Road yardstick itself. A third way, Swank Road from First Fork Road, runs 9.1% for 1.15 km then 8.9% for 1.9 km. Surfaces not confirmed (page: 'state forest dirt or gravel roads'). This site is 4.64 mi south of Trout Run Road on Montour Road, with no further run of 8%+ on that leg, so its best approach is the at-the-yardstick one; kept with the dry-weather caveat and the grades in the note. If 'about the limit, 14 miles from pavement' is too much, this single-site entry is a drop.
Driveway: DIRT, 170 ft, no grade listed; 3DEP road 593.6 m, pin 593.4 m: level. Stays (not grass-steep, not Severe).

DCNR GIS layer vs booking page (ruling 5, kept, both in the note): the GIS record for this site says TrailerAccess 'No'; the booking page lists 'Looking For Category: RV Site, Tent Site, Trailer Site' and a 40-ft maximum vehicle length.

Season written (entry had none): opens 04-01, closes 12-12, from the site page's own statement ('open from the beginning of April through the end of rifle deer season') and 'Status: Open through Sat Dec 12 2026'. The engine's calendar is a little wider at the front: it shows nights Available from early March 2027 (Not Available through 5 March, Available on 11 March; 6-10 March not probed). I wrote the agency's stated April opening; a March night the engine sells is outside the stated season.
